chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Nuh ibn Abdullah, from Al-Dahli, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The good deed (charity/gift) should be initiated (before asking); as for the one you give after he asks, you have merely satisfied him by what he sacrificed his dignity for you. He spends his night awake, restless, standing between hope and despair, not knowing where to turn for his need. Then he resolves to go for it, so he comes to you with his heart quivering and his limbs trembling. You would see his face flushed with blood, not knowing whether he will return with sorrow or with joy.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between giving charity before being asked versus after being asked in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the virtue of *al-Ma'ruf* (initiated kindness) by contrasting it with giving after a request, which often carries an implicit transactional weight. The narration vividly depicts the supplicant’s psychological turmoil—oscillating between hope and despair, with trembling limbs and a racing heart—highlighting the emotional dignity preserved when one gives freely before being asked. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the recipient's honor (*karamah*) through proactive generosity rather than reactive obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, and someone else, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Nuh Bin Abdullah, from Al Zahly, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The goodness, initiate it, and as for the one who gives it after the asking, so rather he has sufficed him after him having sacrificed his face for you, having spent his night swearing, restless, staying between the hope and the despair, not knowing where to face for his needs. Then he determined to go for it, so he came to you and his heart was quivering and his body was shaking, and you would have seen his blood in his face, not knowing whether he would be returning with gloom or with happiness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Idris and others have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn Nuh ibn ‘Abd Allah from al-Dhuhliy in a marfu‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

charity is that which is given before an appeal by the recipient. Giving charity after an appeal by the recipient is compensation for using the dignity of his face when he appealed and his passing the night worried and anxious in hope and despair without knowing which direction to go for his needs. He then decides to come before you with his heart beating fast and his muscles shaking. You can see (the color of) his blood on his face. He does not know whether he will turn back sadly or with happiness.’”
